what: The same baseline party, read off the same panel, once the feed's three lines are spent on what mattered to the domain instead of on what happened last.

theRule.where: HudText.DomainFeed, HudText.DomainSelection and the shared HudText.MostSignificant
theRule.reuseNotReinvention: StorySelection (Issue #140) and DomainSelection (Issue #145) are the same function with one argument changed. MostSignificant takes what counts as one beat; the story passes the reason code, the feed passes the creature id. A copy of the ranking is how the two panels would come to disagree about what matters after the next change to StoryWeight — which is this issue, told forwards: #140 fixed the story panel and left the feed beside it showing the newest three entries.
theRule.step1: one entry per creature — its best by (StoryWeight, LastTick), and the later-written of two that tie
theRule.step2: the crew ordered by the same (StoryWeight, LastTick)
theRule.step3: cut to HudText.DomainFeedLines = 3, then put back in time order, newest first
theRule.fill: routine fills whatever the turning points leave over, so the feed is never blank and the first ~1300 ticks of a party still read as what the crew is doing
theRule.noTickNeeded: every input is a published field of the snapshot and the ranking is a function of the reason code alone. DomainFeedTests.Reading_the_domain_feed_needs_no_tick_to_run builds the panel from a snapshot taken once, steps the world 200 ticks further, and gets the same panel out of the same object.

theScale.question: Issue #145 asks whether the domain's scale of significance differs from one creature's, and to name the difference if it does.
theScale.answer: It does not, and that is a decision rather than an economy. There is no fact in the canonical journal that means something to a domain and nothing to any of its creatures: a domain has no body to be put down and no memory of its own, and every entry it could be told about happened to somebody. HudText.StoryWeight is therefore shared unchanged.
theScale.whatDoesDiffer: What counts as ONE BEAT. For one creature the beat is the kind of decision — the same refusal fourteen times is one line. For the domain the beat is the creature — a creature's whole party is one line, because the domain has nine of them and the question the panel answers is WHO. This is the difference that fixes the measured defect: three lines about one creature stopped in one corridor.
theScale.consequence: The same kind of decision from a second creature is news about a domain; from the same creature it is not. At tick 2400 the feed is three different creatures refusing three different places, where the story panel of any one of them is four different kinds of thing that happened to it.

criterionOne.claim: On the baseline party at tick 2400, sampled every 50 ticks, the share of feed windows carrying at least one entry that mattered is not below the 40% Issue #145 names.
criterionOne.reading: 22 of 48 is the ceiling on this party and not merely a pass: 22 is exactly the number of sampled windows taken at a moment when the party had produced anything that mattered at all. The other 26 windows fall in the first ~1300 ticks, where the journal holds nothing but routine and the feed honestly has nothing to promote.

criterionOneWithNoSlack.claim: At every sampled moment the party has a turning point, the feed carries one.
criterionOneWithNoSlack.before: red — 19 of 22 windows showed nothing that mattered

whatThePanelSaysNow.reading: Without clicking anything, the player is now told that three of the nine crew will not take work at the places where their nerve went, and where and when each of them broke. That is the sentence the whole slice exists for — 'и как это изменило его следующее решение' — on the screen the game opens on. At t1400 the same panel is what the first wave cost: two carried off the floor and one that broke and ran. Before the edit all of it was one creature stopped in one corridor.

whatElseChangedInThePanel.what: The diagnostics counter reads 'Diagnostics: 0' instead of 'Diagnostics: 0 (structured JSON is emitted by smoke/capture).'
whatElseChangedInThePanel.why: Not tidying. A turning-point sentence carries its numbers with it and is longer than a routine one, so three of them need seven drawn lines where three routine ones needed six. With the developer's note the panel measured 11 drawn lines against the 10 its label holds and the screenshots stage of verify.ps1 failed on the prepared party at tick 1670 and on baseline at tick 2400. The note moved into the HudText.Feedback docstring, the count stayed, and the panel is 10 of 10.
whatElseChangedInThePanel.alsoRemoved: the doubled 'EVENT FEEDBACK' header of the empty panel. It was a header concatenated in front of a body that already opened with one; a header that now carries counts cannot be printed twice without lying about them. HudTextTests.An_empty_event_buffer_still_carries_the_header_and_the_diagnostics_count used to assert the doubling with the note 'changing it is a product decision, not a tidy-up' — that decision is made here and written down in the test.

theGoldenFrames.what: The three committed --demo-stone frames, regenerated with scripts/update-golden-ui.ps1 and reviewed rather than accepted.
theGoldenFrames.t190: was three lines of which two were Кремень; is now Кремень, Мотылёк and Смола

theGoldenFrames.note: None of these frames has a turning point in it — 0 mattered on all three — so what changed is only the second half of the rule, one line per creature. That the routine frames improve at all is the part of the fix that has nothing to do with waves.

whatStaysOffTheFeed: six of the nine crew. Measured on this party at tick 2400 all nine have had something that mattered, and three lines is what the frame can draw (evidence/145-bound.json). The header says so: '3 of 9 crew'.
every earlier beat of the three creatures that are shown. A creature's line is its worst moment, not its story; its four beats are one click away on the same panel.
all of the routine while anything else is available — 96.5% of the journal, the number Issue #140 measured and CreatureStoryTests.Most_of_what_a_creature_decides_is_routine keeps honest.

late in a party, everything below a refusal by memory of place. At ticks 2200 and 2400 all three lines are refusals, because three creatures hold the top weight and the panel is three lines long. That is the right three sentences for the hypothesis this slice is testing and it does hide what the fourth wave cost — which a click, or the summary line's crew count, answers.

movement. The feed is a digest and no longer a ticker: ranking by what a decision meant means the top can stand still for hundreds of ticks while the crew works. The summary line above it carries the tick, the wave and the stocks, and the routine fill still moves whenever nothing has mattered yet.
